about: The Azure testbed, one entry per machine. Read by scripts/azure_testbed.py, which prints every command before anything runs. Prices are list prices for planning only; the preflight reads the real CPU limits from the subscription.
location_note: On the free-trial subscription (checked 2026-09-14) North Europe refuses every size below (NotAvailableForSubscription). Sweden Central allows both profiles and was the cheapest of the European regions that do. On the pay-as-you-go subscription (checked 2026-09-15) Italy North and Poland Central also offer the x86 sizes, and only Sweden Central offers the Arm ones. A region allowed 10 CPUs, stopped machines included, until the Sweden Central limits were raised on request on 2026-09-16 to 40 CPUs in total, 20 in the Dav6 family and 10 in the Dpsv6 family. All three pairs therefore fit in Sweden Central, each in its own resource group and network.
public_ip_note: Every machine has a static public address so that it can reach out: on this network (created 2026-09-14) a machine without one had no route to apt or GitHub, and the broker's first boot set up nothing. A public address also matches the Oracle testbed, where every machine had one. Nothing comes in except SSH from the one address the firewall rule names.

matched.about: the Oracle layout the mechanism campaigns ran on: an 8-CPU driver and a 2-CPU broker, on the same AMD EPYC generation (Genoa) as Oracle's E5

arm.about: the materially different machine: the same layout on Azure's Arm chip, one core per CPU

matched-b.about: a second pair of the matched layout, in its own resource group and network, so that two x86 campaigns can run at the same time without sharing a machine

hourly_usd_source: prices.azure.com retail API, Linux pay-as-you-go in swedencentral, read 2026-09-14 and read again unchanged 2026-09-16; disks and public addresses are extra
